_meta.indication: OMONTYS is an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) indicated for the treatment of anemia due to chronic kidney disease (CKD) in adult patients on dialysis

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, active-controlled, open-label, multicenter non-inferiority study; patients randomized 2:1 to Peginesatide IV every 4 weeks vs Epoetin, with a 28-week titration period followed by an 8-week evaluation period
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with anemia due to chronic renal failure on hemodialysis, previously treated with Epoetin (maintenance of Hgb)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change in hemoglobin from baseline to the evaluation period (weeks 29-36), with a non-inferiority margin of 1.0 g/dL
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted mean difference in Hgb change (Peginesatide - Epoetin) = -0.15 g/dL (95% CI -0.30, -0.01); lower limit above -1.0 g/dL, meeting non-inferiority

nct_ctgov.title: Safety & Efficacy of Peginesatide for Maintenance Treatment of Anemia in Participants With Chronic Kidney Disease on Hemodialysis

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, active-controlled, open-label, multicenter non-inferiority study; patients randomized 2:1 to Peginesatide IV or SC every 4 weeks vs Epoetin alfa/beta, 28-week titration then 8-week evaluation period
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with anemia due to CKD on dialysis, previously treated with Epoetin (maintenance of Hgb)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change in hemoglobin from baseline to the evaluation period (weeks 29-36), non-inferiority margin 1.0 g/dL
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted mean difference in Hgb change (Peginesatide - Epoetin) = 0.10 g/dL (95% CI -0.05, 0.26), meeting non-inferiority

nct_ctgov.title: Safety & Efficacy of Peginesatide for Maintenance Treatment of Anemia in Participants With Chronic Kidney Disease on Hemodialysis

key_safety: Most common adverse events (>=10%) are dyspnea (18.4% vs 19.4% epoetin), diarrhea (18.4% vs 15.9%), nausea (17.4% vs 19.6%), cough (15.9% vs 16.6%), and arteriovenous fistula site complication (16.1% vs 16.6%). Boxed/serious risks include increased mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and thromboembolism.
target_moa: Peginesatide is a synthetic pegylated dimeric peptide, unrelated in amino acid sequence to erythropoietin (EPO), that binds to and activates the human erythropoietin receptor, stimulating erythropoiesis

boxed_warning.content: ESAs INCREASE THE RISK OF DEATH, MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION, STROKE, VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM, THROMBOSIS OF VASCULAR ACCESS AND TUMOR PROGRESSION OR RECURRENCE; patients experienced greater risks when administered ESAs to target a hemoglobin level of greater than 11 g/dL

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved to ensure the benefits outweigh the serious risks of potentially fatal cardiovascular and/or thromboembolic adverse events

advisory_committee.vote: Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (December 7, 2011) voted 15 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain that the clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for peginesatide in patients with anemia associated with chronic renal failure on dialysis

summary.text: Standard NDA for a new molecular entity (synthetic ESA) received 5/27/11 and approved on the PDUFA goal date based on four Phase 3 active-controlled non-inferiority trials; approval included a REMS (communication plan) and required postmarketing cardiovascular safety studies. The product was reviewed by the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee, which voted 15-1-1 in favor.

citations.quote: The applicant has submitted an NDA for peginesatide an intravenously and subcutaneously administered synthetic (not biologic) erythropoiesis stimulating agent (ESA).

In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for OMONTYS® (peginesatide) Injection to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the serious risks of potentially fatal cardiovascular and/or thromboembolic adverse events, and the increased risk of these events in patients with CKD not on dialysis.

This product was discussed at a Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on December 7, 2011. The Committee voted 15 (yes), 1 (no), and 1 (abstain) that the available clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for peginesatide for use in patients with anemia associated with chronic renal failure who are on dialysis.
